convoLines.text: "This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Kenneth is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I keep turning over the last thing Kenneth said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them American Ginseng — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"It rewards action, not thought. You learn that fast when you're actually out there instead of theorizing about it."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on the big questions."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Kenneth always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Morgan digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+984 kcal to the pantry.)
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Kenneth died... I keep expecting to see Kenneth at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Sleep's gone strange. I memorize the stars at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Tell you what — Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
Nomsa has an edge today — something curdled.
"Drum-Belly — It rears up, belly swelling drum-taut, and beats it with both paws — BOOM. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"This one — Wild Ramps. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Huh. Let me think about that." Hold it together. That's my whole philosophy. Hold it together.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Arguments cost calories. I do the math out loud until people stop."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what they want. What's the worst that happens."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Jesse sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Why do you ask? I'm not okay. I'm saying it out loud so it's real: I'm not okay."
"Good. Company's company."
"Right, so — My hands stopped shaking. That's — that's something. Thank you for sitting here."
"Still on that hard time."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Wei is gone and Deirdre is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I memorize the stars for Deirdre, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

«मैं नहीं भूलूँगा।» A grin breaks through, quick and warm.

"Still on that plant lesson."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"

"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Alright — I should get back to it."

"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything. It'll pass."
"What's this about? That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"The water goes glass-still. That's The Living Wire telling you it's about to move. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"So — Still on what you believe in."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)

"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"

"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here? Not that it matters."
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Nomsa always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

«यह सच है।» (you catch 'सच' — truth) They nod back, slowly. "Fuck you."

d14: 🕯️ Kenneth Murphy is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.

recoverHome: d15: That night, they bring Kenneth home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d14: At the grave, Morgan speaks for Deirdre — "Kenneth trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
systemVoice: d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
d15: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.

d17: You bury Kenneth. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d17: "Kenneth is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d17: "I keep turning over the last thing Kenneth said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d21: "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Kenneth always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d21: "You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Kenneth died... I keep expecting to see Kenneth at the fire. Stupid."
